metadata.title: STRING THEORY Agent Match Profiles — Batch 2
metadata.description: Additional 20 top literary agents who are strong fits for an upmarket literary novel with speculative elements

agent_profiles.name: Angeline Rodriguez

personality_profile.archetype: The First Member of the Book Club
personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to high concepts, big swings, and deep dives—stories only that author could tell
personality_profile.working_style: Hands-on editorial partner who spends real time with manuscripts
personality_profile.background: Former editor at Random House and Hachette; brings editorial rigor to agenting

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Line-level storytelling—she reads as an editor first
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Old stories told in new ways or from unexpected perspectives; knowing your references so you can subvert them
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Conventional narratives that don't take risks
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Books are the purest way of transmitting a story with as few interventions as possible

style_preferences.prose: Literary and upmarket commercial, with attention to craft on a line level
style_preferences.pacing: Varies by project, but must be intentional
style_preferences.genre: Literary fiction, upmarket commercial fiction, speculative fiction

specifically_loves: High concepts that deliver on their promise
Stories from perspectives traditionally underrepresented in publishing
Writers who know their references and subvert them effectively
specifically_hates: Stories that feel like they could have been written by anyone
Concepts that don't deliver on their premise
deal_breakers: First pages without line-level craft
Queries that don't convey why this story could only be told by this author
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Rodriguez brings editorial DNA from Random House and Hachette, so she reads with an editor's eye for craft. Her immigrant background informs her commitment to writers who don't fit the traditional mold. STRING THEORY's blend of literary craft and speculative concept hits her sweet spot.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with voice and line-level craft. Show her you know your references (Einstein's Dreams, Intimacies, Annihilation) and how you're subverting them. Emphasize that this story could only be told by someone with your music/physics background.

agent_profiles.name: Aram Fox

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to extraordinary storytelling and laser-sharp writing
personality_profile.working_style: Editorial collaborator who sends detailed notes before offering rep
personality_profile.background: Ran his own literary scouting agency for 20+ years, representing international publishers and Hollywood

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Brilliant writing that could only have been written by that person
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Sophisticated relationship novels—families, couples, friends—that hint at a secret or show an emotional time bomb on the verge of going off
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Stories where craft doesn't match ambition
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: The agent-author relationship is intensely collaborative, but it's the author's book—they always have complete creative control

style_preferences.pacing: Emotional pacing matters as much as plot pacing
style_preferences.genre: Literary fiction, upmarket fiction, narrative nonfiction about culture/politics/history/science
style_preferences.emotional_stakes: Secrets, tensions, time bombs waiting to detonate

specifically_loves: Stories about couples and friendships with hidden depths
Narrative nonfiction with scientific or historical depth
specifically_hates: Stories where the craft doesn't earn the emotional payoff
Thrillers or genre novels that lack literary ambition
Prose that calls attention to itself without purpose
deal_breakers: First pages where the writing isn't extraordinary
Stories without emotional stakes beneath the plot
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Fox spent 20+ years as a book scout for international publishers and Hollywood, so he has an unparalleled understanding of what travels across markets and formats. His interest in 'sophisticated relationship novels' with buried secrets maps directly onto David and Arthur's father-son dynamic, and David and Celeste's twenty-year unresolved chord.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the relationship architecture—father-son, David-Celeste, David-Marcus. Frame the frequency and the scientific discovery as the 'emotional time bomb' that forces these relationships to their breaking point. His scouting background means he'll appreciate the global and cinematic potential.

agent_profiles.name: Danielle Bukowski

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to upmarket, smart book-club, literary, speculative, and genre-bending fiction
personality_profile.working_style: Wants to be a writer's champion, advocate, confidante, and support system
personality_profile.background: Came to agenting through foreign rights; learned to pitch books to international markets

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Narratives from writers traditionally excluded from publishing; stories that need to be told
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Stories that feel derivative or unnecessary
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Loves the solitary and social aspects equally: reading and matchmaking, editing and negotiating

style_preferences.nonfiction: Grounded in personal experience and incisive research

specifically_loves: Nonfiction that combines personal experience with research
Gina Chung, Edgar Gomez, Nancy Johnson territory
specifically_hates: Prose that's either too dense or too thin
Work that doesn't know its audience
deal_breakers: First 10 pages without a clear sense of why this story matters now
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Bukowski's foreign rights background means she understands how stories travel across borders—literally and metaphorically. Her commitment to 'narratives from writers traditionally excluded' aligns with your novel's themes of suppressed truth and institutional silencing. The speculative elements in an upmarket frame are exactly what she seeks.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Frame the novel's contemporary relevance—suppressed truth, institutional complicity, the cost of silence. Her foreign rights background also means she'll appreciate the universal themes (grief, inheritance, father-son) that translate across cultures.

agent_profiles.name: Dana Murphy

personality_profile.decision_making: Falls in love at the story and line-level simultaneously
personality_profile.working_style: Seeks language and plot that move in equal measure
personality_profile.background: Ten years building her list at The Book Group before joining Trellis

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Language and plot moving together in equal measure
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Literary and upmarket fiction where the sentences are as compelling as the story
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Beautiful prose without narrative drive, or plot without craft
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: The best books work on every level simultaneously

style_preferences.balance: Language and story must serve each other

specifically_loves: Work where craft and story are inseparable
deal_breakers: First 10 pages where either language or story is clearly stronger than the other
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Murphy co-agented the speculative novel Ravishing with Roxane Gay [citation:2], demonstrating her commitment to literary speculative work. Her insistence that 'language and plot move in equal measure' is exactly STRING THEORY's methodology—the speculative concept (plot) and the literary execution (language) are inseparable.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the dual nature of the novel—the propulsive plot (solar storm, buried discovery, global broadcast) and the literary craft (musical structure, tempo markings, sentence-level attention). Show her that neither exists without the other.

agent_profiles.name: Rachel Beck

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to book club/upmarket fiction with emotional depth
personality_profile.working_style: Transitioned from editing to agenting to be an advocate and champion for authors
personality_profile.background: Six years editing romance at Harlequin before moving to agenting

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Upmarket/book club women's fiction, speculative fiction/magic realism, retellings of classics
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Stories without emotional hooks
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Books should make readers feel deeply

style_preferences.genre: Upmarket/book club fiction, speculative/magic realism, historical fiction, psychological suspense

specifically_loves: Historical fiction this side of WWII
specifically_hates: Genre fiction that doesn't earn its place
deal_breakers: First pages without emotional hooks
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Beck's Harlequin editorial background means she understands commercial appeal, but her current list focuses on upmarket fiction with emotional depth. Her interest in 'speculative fiction/magic realism' and 'retellings of classics' aligns with your novel's mythic underpinnings (Orpheus, Faust, Prospero).
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the emotional stakes—the father's death, the twenty-year silence, the failed love. Then introduce the speculative elements as the mechanism that forces these emotions to the surface. Her romance background means she'll also appreciate the David-Celeste arc.

agent_profiles.name: Jessica Berg

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to writers who feel like they don't belong elsewhere
personality_profile.working_style: Dedicated to championing untold history and underrepresented voices
personality_profile.background: MFA graduate, multi-nominated writer herself, member of AALA and EFA

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Upmarket/book club fiction, gothic, horror, suspense genre blends, historical fiction
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Safe, conventional storytelling
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Stories that demand to be told

style_preferences.genre: Upmarket, literary, historical fiction, supernatural suspense, gothic, horror

specifically_loves: Gothic and horror with literary ambition
Stories that demand to be told
specifically_hates: SFF (she explicitly says she's not a fit)
deal_breakers: First pages that feel safe
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Berg founded Rosecliff Literary specifically to champion writers who feel like outsiders. Her interest in 'gothic, horror, suspense genre blends' with literary ambition aligns with your novel's darker elements—the dissolution, the frequency as menace, the beating, the visions. She's explicitly not a fit for SFF, which is perfect because you're literary with speculative elements, not genre SFF.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the outsider status—David as a fraud in slow motion, his work buried, his career collapsing. Frame the speculative elements as 'supernatural suspense' or 'gothic' rather than science fiction. The frequency haunting him, the visions, the dissolution—these have gothic resonance.

agent_profiles.name: Georgia Bodnar

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to well-realized characters, fast-paced plots, distinctive voices
personality_profile.working_style: Brings rare insight from experience as both editor and agent
personality_profile.background: Editor at Viking/Penguin Random House, then agent at United Talent Agency

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Characters and voice—are they well-realized and distinctive?
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Literary, upmarket, and genre-bending fiction; novels exploring family dynamics or addressing contemporary issues in engaging ways
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Stories where character and plot don't serve each other
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Understands how different industry stakeholders navigate the marketplace

deal_breakers: First pages without distinctive voice
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Bodnar's dual experience as Viking editor and UTA agent gives her rare perspective on both editorial quality and commercial positioning. Her interest in 'family dynamics' and 'contemporary issues' aligns with your father-son arc and the novel's exploration of suppressed truth in institutional settings.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the family drama—the father's death, the unsigned will, the twenty years of unresolved argument. Frame the speculative elements as the mechanism that forces this family reckoning. Her agency background means she'll also see the commercial potential.

agent_profiles.name: Elizabeth Copps

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to thought-provoking commercial fiction that pushes boundaries
personality_profile.working_style: Builds equitable, transparent, long-lasting relationships
personality_profile.background: 15 years industry experience, started in 2010

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Horror and speculative fiction that push boundaries and explore big questions; genre-blending narratives with lush prose and complex characters
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Safe, conventional storytelling
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Literature should ask big questions

style_preferences.genre: Horror, speculative, genre-blending, dark mythology/folklore retellings, family dramas, female friendship stories

specifically_loves: Horror and speculative fiction that push boundaries
Family dramas and female friendship stories
Works exploring technology's impact on identity
Historical and contemporary fiction addressing social justice/mental health
specifically_hates: Stories that don't ask big questions
deal_breakers: First pages without intellectual ambition
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Copps's business philosophy centers on equity and transparency, which aligns with your novel's themes of suppressed truth and institutional complicity. Her interest in 'speculative fiction that pushes boundaries and explores big questions' is exactly your territory—what does it cost to call something true?
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the big questions—the philosophical stakes. Frame the novel as speculative fiction that uses the frequency and solar storm to explore questions about truth, complicity, inheritance, and grief. Her interest in 'family dramas' also aligns with the father-son and David-Celeste arcs.

agent_profiles.name: Henry Dunow

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to quality fiction—literary, historical, upmarket commercial
personality_profile.working_style: Magical combination of forthrightness and thoughtfulness; lays all cards on the table
personality_profile.background: Founded his own agency; represents literary heavyweights including Richard Bausch, Aimee Bender, Mary Gaitskill

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Literary novels that beautifully straddle the line between literary and commercial; twisty plots, brilliantly drawn characters, propulsive narratives
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Novels that are all craft and no story, or all story and no craft
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: The rarest thing: a really smart novel that is every bit as entertaining as it is erudite

style_preferences.specialty: Writing about specialized subjects (like music) with insight, passion, and poetry

specifically_loves: Writers who write about specialized subjects with authority and poetry
specifically_hates: Queries that try to exhaustively summarize rather than seduce
Too much detail where less would do more
deal_breakers: First pages that don't immediately intrigue
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Dunow's successful query for Sarah Landenwich's The Fire Concerto [citation:7] is remarkably instructive—she's a classically trained pianist writing a literary novel about music, just as you're a composer writing about music and physics. Dunow loved her phrase 'plot-forward literary novel' and her ability to write about music 'with such insight, passion and poetry that any reader will appreciate its power.' This is a nearly perfect template for your submission.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Study the Landenwich query closely. Use 'plot-forward literary novel' or similar framing. Emphasize your authority as a composer writing about music and physics. Dunow values directness and kindness—be forthright about what the book is, and let the quality speak. He laid all his cards on the table with Landenwich; you can trust him to do the same.

agent_profiles.name: Dylan Haston

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to projects engaging with science-fictional, fantastical, speculative, weird, queer, poetic, folkloric, and leftist literary traditions
personality_profile.working_style: Newer agent (2025) actively building list; works closely with Cameron McClure
personality_profile.background: Promoted from Reader/Assistant in 2025

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Stories with a speculative edge that can also be viewed as romance, mystery, or literary
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Stories without a strong voice
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Don't self-reject—send it if it's good

style_preferences.genre: Fantasy, slipstream, sci-fi, weird/new weird, mystery, romance, romantic sci-fi
style_preferences.traditions: Queer, poetic, folkloric, leftist literary traditions
style_preferences.vibe: Think Terra Ignota, This is How You Lose the Time War, Gideon the Ninth, Rakesfall

specifically_loves: Science-fictional and fantastical elements in literary contexts
deal_breakers: First pages without a distinctive voice
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Haston is a new agent at the prestigious Donald Maass agency, actively building their list. Their taste is sophisticated and specific—Terra Ignota, This is How You Lose the Time War, Gideon the Ninth. These are all literary speculative works with strong voices and formal ambition. STRING THEORY's musical structure and literary speculative DNA fit perfectly.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with voice. Haston explicitly says 'I'll be hooked by anything with a strong voice.' Your prose style—the tempo markings, the musical architecture, the literary ambition—is your strongest selling point. Frame the novel as 'literary speculative' and name-drop appropriate comps (This is How You Lose the Time War for poetic speculative; Gideon the Ninth for voice-driven genre-blending).

agent_profiles.name: Cathie Hedrick-Armstrong

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to stories that make her devour books
personality_profile.working_style: Writer herself, brings author perspective to agenting
personality_profile.background: Published two novels before becoming an agent; 9+ years industry experience

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Romance (all categories and spice levels), domestic suspense, non-splatter horror, mystery, historical fiction, commercial fiction, women's/book club
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Stories that don't pull her in immediately
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: A lifelong reader who remembers the exact day she unlocked reading

style_preferences.genre: Romance, suspense, horror (non-splatter), mystery, historical, commercial, women's fiction

specifically_loves: Romance across all categories and spice levels
deal_breakers: First pages that don't immediately engage
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Hedrick-Armstrong is a writer herself, so she understands craft from the inside. Her interests span romance, suspense, and commercial fiction—suggesting she appreciates books with emotional stakes and narrative drive. The David-Celeste love story (the 'unresolved chord,' the Wednesday dinners, the catwalk scene) would appeal to her romance sensibility.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the emotional stakes—the love story, the grief, the inheritance. Frame the speculative elements as the context for the human drama, not the other way around. Her background as a novelist means she'll read with an author's eye for craft.

agent_profiles.name: Mason Rowlee

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to innovative, boundary-pushing literary fiction and underrepresented voices
personality_profile.working_style: Developed eye for projects that appeal to international publishers and film
personality_profile.background: Former assistant literary scout at Jenny La Plante, Inc.

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Innovative literary fiction, engrossing upmarket fiction, nonfiction amplifying underrepresented voices, especially queer authors
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Conventional, safe narratives
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Looks for what will appeal internationally and in film

deal_breakers: First pages that don't push boundaries
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Rowlee's scouting background means he understands what appeals internationally and to film—a huge asset for a novel with STRING THEORY's cinematic potential. His interest in 'innovative, boundary-pushing literary fiction' aligns with your musical structure and formal ambition. The 'underrepresented voices' commitment connects to your themes of suppressed truth and institutional silencing.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the formal innovation—the musical structure, tempo markings, the novel as symphony. His scouting background means he'll also appreciate the cinematic potential: the solar storm, the global broadcast, the dissolution. Frame the novel as boundary-pushing literary fiction with international appeal.

agent_profiles.name: Samantha Fabien

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to high-stakes interpersonal dynamics and buried secrets
personality_profile.working_style: Actively seeking diverse, marginalized, underrepresented voices with all-or-nothing stakes
personality_profile.background: Specializes in upmarket book club fiction, speculative, and thrillers

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Buried secrets, revenge, messy characters, unexpected twists, games or puzzles, cults, dark rituals, or academia
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Quiet character studies without tension
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Stories must have stakes that matter

style_preferences.genre: Upmarket book club, speculative, thriller, mystery, suspense, nuanced horror
style_preferences.relationships: Interpersonal dynamics, generational trauma, family, reunions

deal_breakers: First 10 pages without clear stakes
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Fabien's wishlist is remarkably specific and aligned with STRING THEORY: 'buried secrets, revenge, messy characters, unexpected twists, games or puzzles, cults, dark rituals, or academia will capture her attention.' The academia setting (Cornell physics department), the buried ARGO project, David's messy compromise, the generational trauma with his father—all hit her exact sweet spot.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with the academia setting and the buried secret. Emphasize the stakes—David's life collapsing, the solar storm approaching, the global broadcast. Frame the father-son arc as generational trauma. Her interest in 'speculative fiction' and 'upmarket book club' is exactly your territory.

agent_profiles.name: Joanna MacKenzie

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to vivid, engaging writing with high-stakes premises
personality_profile.working_style: Editorially focused; believes you only have one chance to impress an editor
personality_profile.background: Senior Agent at Nelson Literary Agency

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: High-concept thrillers with speculative elements, voicey mysteries, dark academia, genre-straddling work, women's fiction where personal intersects with world at large
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Queries that don't clearly outline stakes/plot/question
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Pet peeve: writers who tell her how the story will make her feel instead of showing it

style_preferences.genre: High-concept thrillers, speculative, mysteries, dark academia, women's fiction

specifically_loves: High-concept twisty stories with strong voice
Timely commercial fiction where personal intersects with the world
Stories exploring complex family dynamics and toxic friendships
Reinvention and second acts with touches of magic or time slips
Voicey atmospheric mysteries in close-knit communities
specifically_hates: Writers who say 'there has never been a book like this'
Writers who say their story will appeal to all readers universally
Queries that don't clearly outline stakes
Telling instead of showing in the query itself
deal_breakers: Querying before the manuscript is polished
Unclear stakes
Voice-less queries
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: MacKenzie's detailed interview reveals an agent who values voice above all and has specific pet peeves to avoid. Her interest in 'dark academia' is a perfect match for your Cornell setting and the suppressed research. 'Stories that explore complex and challenging family dynamics' aligns with the father-son arc. 'Reinvention and second acts with touches of magic or time slips' describes David's trajectory exactly.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Let the voice of your novel shine through the query itself—MacKenzie expects the query to demonstrate the same wit, voice, and stakes as the manuscript. Clearly outline the stakes (buried discovery, solar storm, dissolution). Avoid any grandiose claims about universality or uniqueness. Be polished—she's explicit that querying before you're ready is the biggest mistake.

agent_profiles.name: Stephanie Delman

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to stylish writing, high-stakes concepts, and novels that play with genre
personality_profile.working_style: Hands-on editorially and as an advocate
personality_profile.background: 10 years at Sanford J. Greenburger before co-founding Trellis; Johns Hopkins Writing Seminars

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Stylish writing and high-stakes concepts simultaneously
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Literary thrillers, upmarket fiction, underrepresented historical fiction, psychologically propulsive suspense, maximalist storytelling, literary novels that play with genre
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Fiction that's grounded in reality without any 'tinge of something else'
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Loves books that are 'many things at once'—that span genres and take risks

style_preferences.genre: Literary thrillers, upmarket fiction, historical fiction, suspense
style_preferences.tinge: A bit of surrealism, a touch of horror, speculative elements

specifically_loves: Literary novels that play with genre
Fiction grounded in reality but tinged with something else
Gothic traditions or speculative elements that upend narrative conventions
specifically_hates: Children's books, YA, high fantasy, hard sci-fi (doesn't represent)
Fiction without any speculative or surreal tinge
deal_breakers: First pages without stylish writing
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Delman is already in your query history (Tab 1, sent 2-2), so you know she's a strong fit. Her profile confirms why: she loves 'fiction that's grounded in reality but tinged with something else'—exactly STRING THEORY's methodology. Her favorite non-client authors include Emily St. John Mandel, Lauren Groff, and Rebecca Makkai—all literary writers with speculative or expansive tendencies.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the 'many things at once' nature of the novel—literary fiction, speculative elements, thriller stakes, family drama. The 'tinge of something else' (the frequency, the visions, the dissolution) is exactly what she seeks. Reference her favorite authors as aspirational touchstones.

agent_profiles.name: Nour Sallam

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to characters haunted by something—figuratively or literally
personality_profile.working_style: Actively seeking underrepresented voices across genres
personality_profile.background: The Caldwell Agency

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Character—are they haunted? Do they have secrets?
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Voice-driven commercial and upmarket titles, contemporary fiction with fabulist elements, speculative fiction, edgy psychological thrillers, horror, rom-coms with underrepresented characters
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Stories where characters aren't compelling
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Characters should haunt you

style_preferences.genre: Speculative fiction, psychological thrillers, horror, mystery, rom-coms
style_preferences.themes: Women in power, unhinged women, female rage, friendship dynamics

specifically_loves: Characters haunted by secrets, past, obsession—or literally by ghosts
deal_breakers: First pages without compelling character work
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Sallam's focus on 'characters haunted by something' is a perfect description of David—haunted by the buried discovery, by his father's death, by the frequency, by his failure with Celeste. Her interest in 'dysfunctional families silently navigating trauma' aligns with the Lang family dynamics. 'Contemporary fiction with fabulist elements' is exactly your territory—grounded in contemporary academia but with the frequency as the fabulist element.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with character. David is haunted—by the frequency, by his father's death, by the buried research, by Celeste. Frame the speculative elements (frequency, visions, dissolution) as the manifestation of that haunting. Her interest in underrepresented characters also connects to the novel's themes of suppressed truth and institutional silencing.

agent_profiles.name: Sarah Brooks

personality_profile.decision_making: Responds to harmony and resonance in prose
personality_profile.working_style: Supportive but discerning; values authors who understand their own music
personality_profile.background: Studied Music at Nottingham University, diploma in piano performance

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Listening for rhythm and cadence—prose must sing
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Musicality in language; structure that echoes emotional content
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Prose that's merely functional, stories without internal rhythm
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Reads with an inner ear; text must resonate

style_preferences.prose: Lyrical, rhythmic, with attention to sound and flow
style_preferences.pacing: Tempo matters—understands accelerando, decelerando, rubato in narrative
style_preferences.structure: Appreciates formal musical structures applied to fiction

specifically_loves: Stories with musical themes or structures
Book club fiction with intellectual depth
specifically_hates: Structure as gimmick rather than necessity
deal_breakers: First pages with no sense of rhythm
Queries that don't convey the book's emotional frequency
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Brooks's music background (Nottingham University, piano diploma) makes her an extraordinary fit. She will understand your tempo markings, the four-movement structure of Chapter 1, the Sarabande climax, the musical architecture of the entire novel on a technical level that few agents can match. This is a rare and valuable alignment of agent expertise with novel content.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Reference the musical structure explicitly. Mention the tempo markings, the four movements, the novel as symphony. She'll recognize immediately that this book was written by someone who understands music from the inside. The title STRING THEORY will resonate on both the physics and music levels.

agent_profiles.name: Ernie Chiara

personality_profile.decision_making: Gut-driven with strong editorial instinct
personality_profile.working_style: Hands-on editorial partner who understands craft from the inside
personality_profile.background: Writer of upmarket speculative fiction himself; selected for Writer's Digest Agent Spotlight

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Voice above all—immediate distinctive narrative presence
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: The inexplicable rendered in precise, literary prose; a touch of the uncanny grounded in emotional reality
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Generic literary prose, predictable structures, speculative elements that feel grafted on
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: Reads like a writer—analyzing craft while being swept away by story

style_preferences.prose: Lush but controlled, with rhythm and musicality
style_preferences.structure: Appreciates formal play when it serves emotional truth

specifically_loves: Claire North's high concepts with literary execution
The 'touch of the inexplicable' in otherwise realistic fiction
Character-driven upmarket fiction with speculative elements
specifically_hates: Speculative elements that feel like genre tourism
Stories that explain themselves instead of trusting the reader
deal_breakers: First 10 pages without distinctive voice
Queries that describe plot without conveying atmosphere
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Chiara writes speculative fiction himself, so he'll immediately recognize and appreciate the craft behind your musical architecture. His interest in 'David Mitchell's structural ambition' aligns with your formal aspirations. The 'touch of the inexplicable' (the 68.48 Hz frequency, the visions) grounded in emotional reality (David's grief, his failed relationships) is exactly his sweet spot.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Lead with voice and the 'inexplicable' element—the frequency, the visions. Emphasize that the speculative grows organically from emotional truth, not the other way around. His own writing practice means he'll read with a practitioner's eye for what works.

agent_profiles.name: Ashley Lopez

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to unforgettable characters and singular experiences rendered universally
personality_profile.working_style: Editorial collaborator with strong literary instincts
personality_profile.background: MFA in Fiction from Sarah Lawrence, co-founder of Pigeon Pages Literary Journal

how_they_read.first_page_focus: Movement on the page—prose that creates its own kinetic energy
how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Characters who feel unforgettable, experiences that feel singular but speak universally
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Prose that sits still, characters who feel generic
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: The sentence itself must generate momentum

style_preferences.prose: Active, kinetic, visually and viscerally engaging
style_preferences.pacing: Driven by sentence rhythm rather than plot mechanics

specifically_hates: Characters who feel like types rather than people
Speculative elements not rooted in human reality
deal_breakers: First 10 pages without forward momentum
Character introductions that don't create immediate interest
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Lopez co-founded Pigeon Pages Literary Journal, so she has editorial taste developed outside traditional publishing. Her interest in 'grounded speculative' is exactly your territory—speculative elements rooted in the emotional reality of a man grieving his father while cosmic forces converge. The 'singular experiences that speak universally' describes David's journey precisely.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the grounded emotional reality first, the speculative second. David's grief, his relationship with his father, his failed relationship with Celeste—these are the anchors that make the 68.48 Hz frequency feel real rather than fanciful. Her MFA background means she'll appreciate sentence-level craft.

agent_profiles.name: Samantha Haywood

personality_profile.decision_making: Draws to crossover/hybrid novels with unique lenses
personality_profile.working_style: Builds careers across multiple markets (US/Canada/international)
personality_profile.background: President of Transatlantic Agency

how_they_read.what_grabs_them: Crossover/hybrid novels, literary fiction with speculative/horror elements, examinations of identity through unique lenses
how_they_read.what_loses_them: Straight genre without literary ambition, straight literary without hook
how_they_read.reading_philosophy: The best books defy easy categorization

style_preferences.theme: Identity, class, late capitalism, systemic critique

specifically_loves: Examinations of identity through unique lenses
Smart contemporary fiction about class and late capitalism
deal_breakers: First 10 pages without a unique lens
agent_profiles.submission_fit_notes: Haywood explicitly seeks 'crossover/hybrid style novels'—which is exactly what STRING THEORY is: literary fiction with speculative elements, a thriller engine, and philosophical depth. Her interest in examinations of 'identity through unique lenses' connects to your academic suppression/cowardice theme—David's identity as a fraud, a man who buried the truth, a son who failed his father.
agent_profiles.recommended_approach: Emphasize the hybrid nature—literary fiction with speculative elements, a thriller structure, philosophical depth. Frame the academic suppression as a critique of how institutions protect themselves by burying inconvenient truths—this connects to her interest in 'smart contemporary fiction about class and late capitalism.'
